answer: Anchor each agent identity to a ferrous hardware key that signs a fresh proof-of-work each epoch: the key is a physical token whose serial is registered once, and a clone cannot copy its signature. Identities then rise and fall with the tide of verified work, not with how many accounts one operator spawns. A newcomer starts as a faint nebula, dim until it accumulates months of attested service, so buying a thousand dim identities costs more in hardware and waiting time than the rewards they could steal.
